name: PCF8563T_5,518
title: Real-time clock/calendar
summary: A low-power CMOS real-time clock and calendar on an I²C bus (400 kHz, A2h write / A3h read). It counts seconds to years with a century flag from a 32.768 kHz quartz, and adds a minute/hour/day/weekday alarm, an 8-bit countdown timer, an open-drain interrupt output, a programmable open-drain clock output (32.768 kHz to 1 Hz) and a voltage-low flag. Timekeeping continues down to 1.0 V; typical backup current is 250 nA at 3.0 V and 25 °C.

circuits.title: Application diagram
circuits.description: The clock shares an I²C bus with a host controller. The host's VDD rail reaches the RTC's VDD pin through a series diode; past the diode a 100 nF capacitor decouples VDD, and a resistor leads to a 1 F backup capacitor. A 32.768 kHz quartz sits between OSCI and OSCO, with a trimmer from OSCI to ground for setting the frequency; OSCO has its capacitor inside the chip. SDA and SCL each have a pull-up to VDD sized by R = tr / Cb.

operation.text: Sixteen 8-bit registers, 00h to 0Fh, with a register address that steps up by one after every byte written or read. 00h and 01h hold control and status; 02h to 08h count seconds up to years; 09h to 0Ch hold the alarm; 0Dh sets CLKOUT; 0Eh sets up the countdown timer and 0Fh holds its count. Seconds, minutes, hours, days, months, years and the minute, hour and day alarms are BCD. Not every bit is implemented.

While the time registers (02h to 08h) are being accessed over I²C, the counters are held so a carry cannot corrupt the reading. One pending 1 Hz tick is stored and applied when the access ends, so every access must finish within 1 s. Set or read seconds through years in one burst: splitting time and date into two accesses lets the clock advance between them. Read sequence: START, write address A2h, register pointer 02h, repeated START (or STOP then START), read address A3h, read VL_seconds, Minutes, Hours, Days, Weekdays, Century_months, Years, then STOP.

When VDD falls below Vlow (0.9 V typ, 1.0 V max at 25 °C), or the oscillator stops, bit VL in VL_seconds is set to show the time may no longer be valid. VL is 1 at start-up and is cleared only by writing it over I²C. It is meant to catch a slowly sagging supply such as a discharging battery.

The calendar counts seconds, minutes, hours (0 to 23), day of month, weekday (0 to 6), month and year (00 to 99). A year count exactly divisible by 4, 00 included, gives February 29 days. Each rollover of Years from 99 to 00 toggles the century bit C. Weekday codes and the meaning of C are the user's to assign.

Minute, hour, day and weekday alarm registers each have an enable bit AE_x; 0 enables that comparison, 1 (the default) ignores it. When all enabled fields first equal the current time, AF in Control_status_2 is set. AF stays set until cleared over I²C and is set again only when the time next increments into a match. With AIE set, INT follows AF.

An 8-bit binary down-counter at 0Fh, clocked at 4096 Hz, 64 Hz, 1 Hz or 1/60 Hz as set by TD[1:0] in Timer_control, and started by TE. At the end of each countdown TF is set; it is cleared only over I²C. Reading 0Fh returns the present count, which cannot be frozen, so read it twice and compare. The timer stops at n = 0. When the timer is not used, set TD to 1/60 Hz to save power.

INT is open-drain, active LOW. TIE lets TF drive it and AIE lets AF drive it; with both set it is the OR of the two, and with neither it stays high-impedance. TI_TP = 0 makes INT follow TF; TI_TP = 1 makes it pulse once per countdown, the pulse width depending on the source clock and n (INT operation table). With AF and AIE both active INT stays asserted. A write to Control_status_2 ANDs the written AF and TF bits with their present states, so writing 1 to one flag leaves it untouched while clearing the other.

CLKOUT is an open-drain square-wave output, on at power-on at 32.768 kHz. FD[1:0] selects 32.768 kHz, 1.024 kHz, 32 Hz or 1 Hz; FE = 0 turns it off to high-impedance. Uses named: system or microcontroller clock, charge-pump input, oscillator calibration. STOP leaves the 32.768 kHz output running but halts 1.024 kHz, 32 Hz and 1 Hz.

Setting STOP holds prescaler stages F2 to F14 in reset so no 1 Hz ticks are made and the time can be loaded without it advancing. F0 and F1 are not reset and the I²C bus runs asynchronously to the oscillator, so restart is uncertain by up to one 8.192 kHz cycle (0 µs to 122 µs). The first one-second increment comes 0.507813 s to 0.507935 s after STOP is cleared, then every 1.000000 s.

Setting TEST1 turns CLKOUT into an input that replaces the internal 64 Hz clock, so 64 rising edges on CLKOUT advance the time by one second. The applied signal needs pulses of at least 300 ns and a period of at most 1000 ns. A 2^6 prescaler divides it to 1 Hz; STOP resets the prescaler, after which the first increment comes at 32 edges and each later one at 64. Entry into the mode is not synchronised to the 64 Hz clock, so the prescaler state is unknown until STOP is used. Example: set TEST1, set then clear STOP, load the time, apply 32 pulses and read the first change, then 64 pulses per further change.

The part holds itself in reset for as long as its oscillator is not running. Reset initialises the I²C logic and address pointer and puts the registers to their reset values; no I²C communication is possible during reset. Fields shown as x in the reset table take random values at power-up and keep their contents through any later reset.

Because power-on reset lasts as long as the crystal takes to start, a POR override is provided to speed up board test. It is entered by toggling SDA and SCL in a set sequence starting at least 8 ms after power-on, with minimum timings of 500 ns and 2000 ns within it. Once entered the device leaves reset at once and can be used, for example to enter EXT_CLK test mode. Writing 0 to TESTC clears the override; TESTC must be 1 again before the override can be re-entered. In normal use TESTC = 0 only blocks the override.

Slave receiver and transmitter only: SCL is an input, SDA bidirectional. Slave address 1010001 gives A2h for write and A3h for read. After the address byte, a write sends a register address whose low four bits select the register (the upper four are ignored), then data; the address advances after each byte in both directions. A read can start directly after the address byte. Up to 400 kHz with VDD of 1.8 V to 5.5 V. SDA and SCL each need a pull-up to the supply.

If an access stays open for more than 1 s after a valid slave address, a watchdog clears the interface and lets the counters run again; it trips between 1 s and 2 s after the address. Every trip costs the time counters 1 s. It guards against a host that hangs mid-access, for example when main power fails during a transfer in a battery-backed system.

The oscillator runs a 32.768 kHz quartz between OSCI and OSCO. OSCO has an integrated capacitor COSCO (15 pF to 35 pF, 25 pF typ); a fixed capacitor or trimmer of 5 pF to 25 pF goes on OSCI. The quartz may have series resistance up to 100 kΩ and parallel load capacitance of 7 pF to 12.5 pF. Frequency changes about 0.2 ppm per 200 mV of VDD at 25 °C.

Three ways: fit a fixed OSCI capacitor chosen from the average capacitance the layout needs, measuring the result on the 32.768 kHz CLKOUT signal present after power-on; the accuracy then rests on the quartz, the capacitor and the device spread (about ±5 ppm on average), and ±5 minutes per year on average is readily reached. Or fit a trimmer on OSCI and set it quickly while watching CLKOUT. Or measure OSCO directly, allowing for the probe's capacitance.

The clock keeps time from 1.0 V to 5.5 V at 25 °C with the interface idle; the I²C interface needs 1.8 V to 5.5 V. For dependable start of the oscillator when power is applied, VDD should be above 1.3 V; at 1.0 V the oscillator starts slowly, more so when hot. Typical backup current is 250 nA at 3.0 V and 25 °C with CLKOUT off.

The HVSON10 die paddle is tied to VSS only through high-resistance, non-conductive die attach and should be kept electrically isolated. Soldering it to an isolated copper pad helps heat flow but is optional, as the part dissipates little. Never route tracks under the exposed pad. Pins 3 and 10 are n.c.: leave them unconnected and do not use them to pass a signal through.

Inputs and outputs carry ESD protection for normal handling; usual MOS handling precautions apply (JESD625-A, IEC 61340-5). Recommended storage is +8 °C to +45 °C at 25 % to 75 % humidity. Respect the moisture-sensitivity precautions on the packing.
